cmyk.description: A CMYK colour: cyan, magenta, yellow and black in that order, each a percentage of ink from 0 to 100, e.g. [0, 100, 100, 0] for a red.

spot.description: A spot (named) ink colour with the CMYK that prints in its place.

fallback.description: The CMYK that prints and separates in place of the spot ink; it is what reaches the plate.

cmyk.description: A CMYK colour: cyan, magenta, yellow and black in that order, each a percentage of ink from 0 to 100, e.g. [0, 100, 100, 0] for a red.

name.description: The spot colour's name as the print shop knows it, e.g. a Pantone name.

preview.description: How a screen paints the spot, as an RGB colour. Never what prints.

rgb.description: An RGB colour: red, green and blue in that order, each on the 0 to 255 scale, e.g. [255, 0, 0] for red.

ink.description: One of the tenant's inks, by its id, as the ink library lists it.

entry.description: The linked entry's id within that palette, `pe_…`, as get_palette returns it. The colour follows the entry.

palette.description: The linked palette's id, `pal_…`, as list_palettes returns it.

kind.description: color paints the whole artwork, bleed included; image fills it with a picture.

crop.description: Where the picture sits in its frame, under cover. Absent is uncropped.

maxZoom.description: The most zoom a customer may choose; absent is 3.

minZoom.description: The least zoom a customer may choose; absent is 1.

value.description: The attribute's value, as the template stores it.

xFrac.description: How far the picture's centre sits right of the frame's centre, in frame widths: 0.1 is a tenth of the frame. Clamped so the picture always covers the frame, never refused.

yFrac.description: How far the picture's centre sits below the frame's centre, in frame heights: 0.1 is a tenth of the frame. Clamped so the picture always covers the frame, never refused.

zoom.description: The picture's scale over what cover gives it: 1 is the picture just covering the frame, up to 5.

fit.description: How the picture fills its box: cover crops, contain shows it whole, fill stretches, tile repeats it. Absent is cover.

coverAlign.description: Which of nine points, top-left to bottom-right, the artwork is held at in a print box of another shape: what a cover crop keeps, or where a contained artwork sits with the spare space opposite it. Not read under fill. Absent is center.

image.description: Whether, and how, a customer may add image layers.

layer.description: The preset every added image layer starts as: a image layer without id, name, z, anchorTo, locked, print or deletable. What it offers is what a customer may change on the layers they add.

anchor.description: The point of the reference the layer is placed against, and the layer's own matching point: top-left puts the layer's top-left corner on the reference's.

hFrac.description: The layer's height as a fraction of the reference's height. Positive; uncapped, so above 1 hangs over the edge and is clipped.

mat.description: A backdrop painted behind this layer's content at exactly its box: a colour, or a filled shape. Text and image layers only.

textBox.description: What the text layer does when its text does not fit its box. Every size here is a fraction of the plate.

breakWords.description: true breaks a word wider than the box across lines rather than refusing it.

mode.description: adapt keeps the font size and grows the box, then shrinks the text, as far as the limits below allow.

order.description: Which way the box grows first. Absent is widerFirst.

shrinkTo.description: The smallest font size the text may shrink to, as a fraction of the plate's height. Absent, it does not shrink.

tallerTo.description: How tall the box may grow, as a fraction of the plate's height, at most 1. Absent, it does not grow taller.

then.description: What happens to text that still does not fit: clamp cuts it at the box, reject refuses the text.

widenTo.description: How wide the box may grow, as a fraction of the plate's width, at most 1. Absent, it does not widen.

max.description: The largest font size, as a fraction of the plate's height; null is no limit, as large as one line of the box.

min.description: The smallest font size, as a fraction of the plate's height.

mode.description: fill sizes the text to fill the box, between min and max.

then.description: What happens to text that still does not fit: clamp cuts it at the box, reject refuses the text.

textPath.description: A curve the text runs along, as one line: absent is straight lines. The text box still fits it along the curve's length: it shrinks, then is cut or refused, never widening or growing taller.

centerDeg.description: Where the text's run is centred, in degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock: 0 is the top, 90 the right, 180 the bottom.

side.description: Which side of the curve the letters stand on: outside reads clockwise round it (the top of a badge); inside hangs inside it and runs the other way, so text at the bottom reads left to right.

sweepDeg.description: How much of the oval the arc covers, in degrees, above 0 and at most 360: 360 is a whole circle.

type.description: Along the oval inside the layer's box, a circle when the box is square: the box is the radius.

dFrac.description: SVG path data in fractions of its box, (0,0) its top-left and (1,1) its bottom-right: `M 0 0 L 1 0 L 1 1 L 0 1 Z` is the whole box. No arcs.

wFrac.description: The layer's width as a fraction of the reference's width. Positive; uncapped, so above 1 hangs over the edge and is clipped.

max.description: How many text layers a customer may add, 1 to 20.

place.description: Where the added text layers show in the customer's form: in a group, before or after one of its layers, or after its last. Absent, in a step of their own after the template's.

after.description: The id of the group's layer they come after.

before.description: The id of the group's layer they come before.

group.description: The id of the group the added text layers show in.

dpi.description: The resolution the artwork is drawn at, in dots per inch; 300 is usual for print.

drawAtTemplateRatio.description: true: the customer's canvas keeps the ratio at every print size, and the print is cropped or banded by fit. Absent is false.

fallbackFamily.description: The family of `fonts` a character a text's own family lacks is drawn in, at the text's weight and style: the tenant's default font family when the version was published.

fit.description: How the artwork sits in a print box of another shape: contain, cover or fill.

anchor.description: The point of the reference the layer is placed against, and the layer's own matching point: top-left puts the layer's top-left corner on the reference's.

anchorTo.description: Another layer's id, to place and size this one against that layer's box instead of the plate. A missing layer falls back to the plate.

blend.description: How it mixes with the layers under it, per ink. Absent is normal.

deletable.description: true lets a customer delete the layer from their design.

hFrac.description: The layer's height as a fraction of the reference's height. Positive; uncapped, so above 1 hangs over the edge and is clipped.

id.description: The layer's id: what anchorTo, groups and a customer's values name it by. Never changes.

locked.description: true locks the layer on the author's canvas: clicks pass through and it cannot be deleted. Absent is unlocked.

mat.description: A backdrop painted behind this layer's content at exactly its box: a colour, or a filled shape. Text and image layers only.

then.description: What happens to text that still does not fit: clamp cuts it at the box, reject refuses the text.

hFrac.description: The layer's height as a fraction of the reference's height. Positive; uncapped, so above 1 hangs over the edge and is clipped.

id.description: The layer's id: what anchorTo, groups and a customer's values name it by. Never changes.

locked.description: true locks the layer on the author's canvas: clicks pass through and it cannot be deleted. Absent is unlocked.

name.description: What the author reads the layer as. Not unique; absent, the layer reads as its id.

offsetFrac.description: How far the layer sits from its anchor, as fractions of the reference, always toward the reference's centre: { x: 0.05, y: 0.05 } nudges it 5 % in from any corner. Ignored on a centred axis.

x.description: Across, as a fraction of the reference's width: 0.05 is 5 %. Toward the centre; negative pushes outward. Uncapped.

y.description: Down or up, as a fraction of the reference's height: 0.05 is 5 %. Toward the centre; negative pushes outward. Uncapped.

opacity.description: The layer's opacity, which a customer may be offered. Absent is full and not offered.

constraints.description: What a customer may choose, when editable. Absent, the attribute's own range.

max.description: The most opacity a customer may choose, 0.01 to 1.

min.description: The least opacity a customer may choose, 0.01 to 1.

step.description: The step between choosable opacities, e.g. 0.05.

description.description: A hint shown to the customer under the attribute's field.

editable.description: Whether a customer may change it. A layer is customer-editable when any of its attributes is.

fieldKey.description: The author's word for the field (`name`, `photo`), unique within the template. A customer's value for a keyed field follows them to any template with a field of the same key.

label.description: What a customer reads the attribute as, when editable.

value.description: How opaque the whole layer is: 1 is full, 0.01 the least.

print.description: false makes it a guide layer: laid out and drawn on the author's canvas, never printed or shown to a customer. Absent prints.

crop.description: Where the picture sits in its frame, under cover. Absent is uncropped.

constraints.description: What a customer may choose, when editable. Absent, the attribute's own range.

maxZoom.description: The most zoom a customer may choose; absent is 3.

minZoom.description: The least zoom a customer may choose; absent is 1.

xFrac.description: How far the picture's centre sits right of the frame's centre, in frame widths: 0.1 is a tenth of the frame. Clamped so the picture always covers the frame, never refused.

yFrac.description: How far the picture's centre sits below the frame's centre, in frame heights: 0.1 is a tenth of the frame. Clamped so the picture always covers the frame, never refused.

zoom.description: The picture's scale over what cover gives it: 1 is the picture just covering the frame, up to 5.

fill.description: What the silhouette is painted with: a colour, a gradient across its box, or a picture clipped to it.

allowUpload.description: Whether a customer may upload a picture of their own.

anyColor.description: true lets a customer choose any colour, beside or instead of a palette.

cutOut.description: true cuts a customer's upload out onto a transparent background, as a new upload in its place paid from the tenant's credits; one that fails leaves their photo as it was. Absent, never.

oneOf.description: The values a customer may choose from, when the attribute is editable: font families, picture asset ids, shape ids (`shp_…`) or fits. Absent, any value the attribute takes.

palette.description: The palette a customer picks from: one of your palettes' ids (`pal_…`) in a template you write; its name, with the palette under `palettes`, in a published template as served.

requireChange.description: Whether a customer must change the template's default (a placeholder name or photo) before a design is accepted. Only on an offered text's content, image's picture, or shape's outline or fill.

required.description: Whether a customer must choose a picture.

upscale.description: Present, an upload below `belowDpi` at the customer's chosen size is offered an upscale to `toDpi` before the proof, paid from the tenant's credits. Absent, never.

belowDpi.description: The print resolution, in dots per inch, below which an upload is offered an upscale. Absent, the template's minimum, else the tenant's.

toDpi.description: The print resolution, in dots per inch, an upload is upscaled to, and priced by: under `belowDpi`, at it or past it. Absent, `belowDpi`.

mode.description: adapt keeps the font size and grows the box, then shrinks the text, as far as the limits below allow.

order.description: Which way the box grows first. Absent is widerFirst.

shrinkTo.description: The smallest font size the text may shrink to, as a fraction of the plate's height. Absent, it does not shrink.

tallerTo.description: How tall the box may grow, as a fraction of the plate's height, at most 1. Absent, it does not grow taller.

then.description: What happens to text that still does not fit: clamp cuts it at the box, reject refuses the text.

widenTo.description: How wide the box may grow, as a fraction of the plate's width, at most 1. Absent, it does not widen.

then.description: What happens to text that still does not fit: clamp cuts it at the box, reject refuses the text.

textPath.description: A curve the text runs along, as one line: absent is straight lines. The text box still fits it along the curve's length: it shrinks, then is cut or refused, never widening or growing taller.

centerDeg.description: Where the text's run is centred, in degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock: 0 is the top, 90 the right, 180 the bottom.

side.description: Which side of the curve the letters stand on: outside reads clockwise round it (the top of a badge); inside hangs inside it and runs the other way, so text at the bottom reads left to right.

sweepDeg.description: How much of the oval the arc covers, in degrees, above 0 and at most 360: 360 is a whole circle.

type.description: Along the oval inside the layer's box, a circle when the box is square: the box is the radius.

textBox.description: What the text layer does when its text does not fit its box. Every size here is a fraction of the plate.

mode.description: adapt keeps the font size and grows the box, then shrinks the text, as far as the limits below allow.

order.description: Which way the box grows first. Absent is widerFirst.

shrinkTo.description: The smallest font size the text may shrink to, as a fraction of the plate's height. Absent, it does not shrink.

tallerTo.description: How tall the box may grow, as a fraction of the plate's height, at most 1. Absent, it does not grow taller.

then.description: What happens to text that still does not fit: clamp cuts it at the box, reject refuses the text.

widenTo.description: How wide the box may grow, as a fraction of the plate's width, at most 1. Absent, it does not widen.

textPath.description: A curve the text runs along, as one line: absent is straight lines. The text box still fits it along the curve's length: it shrinks, then is cut or refused, never widening or growing taller.

centerDeg.description: Where the text's run is centred, in degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock: 0 is the top, 90 the right, 180 the bottom.

side.description: Which side of the curve the letters stand on: outside reads clockwise round it (the top of a badge); inside hangs inside it and runs the other way, so text at the bottom reads left to right.

sweepDeg.description: How much of the oval the arc covers, in degrees, above 0 and at most 360: 360 is a whole circle.

x.description: Across, as a fraction of the reference's width: 0.05 is 5 %. Toward the centre; negative pushes outward. Uncapped.

y.description: Down or up, as a fraction of the reference's height: 0.05 is 5 %. Toward the centre; negative pushes outward. Uncapped.

info.description:
# Overview

The Pixonaut API turns a template into a printed product. A merchant publishes
templates; a customer fills one in inside the designer on the merchant's
storefront and commits a **design**; the merchant's own server approves the
design, **prints** it, and sends the print to a printshop as an **order**.
Each of those steps is also reported as an **event**, delivered to the
merchant's webhook endpoints.

Start with [Design to order](#tag/design-to-order), which walks through that
flow request by request.

## Base URL

This reference names no server. Send requests to the host that serves it:
the same origin as its `/openapi.json`. Every example path in it is relative
to that host.

## Versions

The routes an integration calls are under `/v1`, and the version is the path
prefix. A few routes sit outside it because they are fetched as plain URLs
rather than called: template images under `/t`, and the signed links the API
hands out for print files, proof images, uploads and published assets.

## Requests and responses

Bodies are JSON, sent with `content-type: application/json`, unless a route
says otherwise (an upload's bytes, an image, a PDF). Times are milliseconds
since the Unix epoch unless a field says otherwise. Every route in this
reference lists the key it takes, its request and response shapes, and each
refusal it can answer with.

## Operation names

Every operation has an `operationId` of the form `<resource>.<verb>`, nested
resources dotted: `templates.list`, `designs.approve`,
`blanks.placements.fittingTemplates.list`. The SDKs name their methods from
it, so `templates.list` is `client.templates.list()` in JavaScript and
`$client->templates->list()` in PHP. The routes outside `/v1`, which are
fetched as plain URLs, are named too and carry `x-sdk-skip: true`: no SDK
generates a method for them.

# Authentication

A route that takes an API key reads it as a bearer token:

```http
Authorization: Bearer sk_...
```

A tenant has three kinds of key, and every such route says which it takes. The
few routes that take no key are signed links the API hands out, which carry
their own proof, and public files; they are listed with the rest below.

## Publishable key

A publishable key (`pk_...`) is meant to sit in a browser, inside the designer on the merchant's own storefront, so it is visible to anyone who opens the page. It is bound to the web origins the tenant allows, and refused from any other. It can do what a customer needs: read templates, preview, upload a picture and commit a design. It cannot approve, print or order.

A request with a publishable key must carry an `Origin` header matching one
of the key's `allowedOrigins` (set when the key is created with
`POST /v1/api-keys`), or it is refused with `origin_forbidden`. An entry is
an exact origin (`https://shop.example`), or `*.shop.example`, which matches
`shop.example` and any subdomain of it. An entry of `*` alone matches every
origin, which removes the key's origin binding altogether: any page on any
site can then use it, so it is for trying the API out, never for a live
storefront. Because a browser sets `Origin`
itself, a publishable key sent from a server with no `Origin` is refused too:
a server uses its secret key, and a connected store's server its integration
key.

## Secret key

A secret key (`sk_...`) stays on the merchant's server. It acts as the tenant itself, and it is the only credential that approves designs, prints them and submits orders.

Never send it to a browser. Revoke one with `DELETE /v1/api-keys/{id}` when
whoever holds it no longer should.

## Integration key

An integration key (`ik_...`) is a connected store's key, given to the store when a member approves its connection, together with a publishable key and a webhook endpoint. It stays on the store's server and acts as the tenant, but only within its grants: it reads templates, blanks and printshops, makes and decides designs, makes and reads prints, places and reads orders, and manages the one webhook endpoint it was given. It never registers another endpoint or reaches one it was not given, and never manages keys, members, roles or settings. Pixel in the store's admin and the MCP endpoint act as a member, so they take the member key a store's user links instead (`member_link_required`).

A store gets one by connecting: the merchant starts at the store, approves in
the studio, and the store exchanges the code it is sent back with for its
integration key, a publishable key bound to the store's origin and a webhook
endpoint at the store (`POST /v1/connect/token`). Nobody copies a key by
hand. A route the key's grants do not cover refuses it with `forbidden`.
`DELETE /v1/connect` disconnects the store: it revokes all three.

## Member key

A member key (`mk_...`) is held by a connected store for one of its users, who linked their own Pixonaut account to it (`POST /v1/connect/token` with `kind: "member_link"`). It acts as that member, with their permissions: Pixel in the store's admin, with the conversation theirs in that store, and the MCP endpoint, as an MCP key the member minted would. It holds while the link, the store's connection and the membership do; after that it is refused `member_link_revoked`.

A store links one of its users the way it connects: it sends the user to the
studio with `kind=member_link`, the member approves linking themselves to the
workspace the store is connected to, and the store exchanges the code with its
integration key as the bearer (`POST /v1/connect/token` with
`kind: "member_link"`). The store that connects is given its approving
member's key in the same exchange (`memberKey`). The store keeps the key for
that user and sends it on Pixel's routes and the MCP endpoint, which refuse
the integration key itself with `member_link_required`.
`DELETE /v1/connect/member-link` unlinks it.

## Share link

A share link's token (`link_...`), such as the one in a correction link a store mints for its customer (`POST /v1/designs/{id}/correction-links`), sent by the hosted page the link opens. The token is the credential; the api takes it only from the hosted pages' origin (their `Origin` header, or none on a read the page sends to its own origin), and a correction link also from the tenant's store origins, which keeps other web pages from using a link in a browser. A link acts only on its own template, design or session, and a designer link reads the blank it is sold on: any other is answered as not found.

A store never sends this token itself: it hands the link to its customer,
and the hosted page sends the token. It is listed on every route a link
reaches, so a client validating what a hosted page sends can check it.

## Which key each group of routes takes

The number of routes in each group that take a publishable key, a secret key,
an integration key, a member key, a share link, or no key at all. A route with no key is a signed link the API handed out,
which carries its own proof, or a public file.

| Group | Publishable key | Secret key | Integration key | Share link | Member key | No key |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API keys | none | 4 of 11 | 6 of 11 | none | 1 of 11 | 1 of 11 |
| Assets | 6 of 27 | 19 of 27 | none | 6 of 27 | none | 4 of 27 |
| Automations | none | all | none | none | none | none |
| Blanks | 4 of 9 | 8 of 9 | 7 of 9 | 3 of 9 | none | 1 of 9 |
| Designs | 1 of 27 | all | all | 11 of 27 | none | none |
| Events | none | all | all | none | none | none |
| Fonts | none | none | none | none | none | all |
| Orders | none | all | 14 of 17 | 6 of 17 | none | none |
| Pixel | 1 of 7 | none | none | 1 of 7 | 6 of 7 | none |
| Prints | none | 6 of 8 | 6 of 8 | none | none | 2 of 8 |
| Printshops | none | all | all | none | none | none |
| Proofs | 3 of 4 | 3 of 4 | none | 3 of 4 | none | 1 of 4 |
| Sessions | 1 of 2 | all | none | 1 of 2 | none | none |
| Share links | none | all | all | none | none | none |
| Templates | 6 of 8 | all | 5 of 8 | 3 of 8 | none | none |
| Webhook endpoints | none | all | 7 of 8 | none | none | none |

# Errors

A refused request answers a 4xx or 5xx status with a JSON body whose `error`
is a code, and sometimes fields that say more:

<!-- example: POST /v1/prints 409 -->
```json
{ "error": "design_not_approved" }
```

<!-- example: POST /v1/designs 422 -->
```json
{ "error": "payload_too_large", "maxBytes": 65536, "bytes": 70312 }
```

Branch on `error`, never on the status alone: one status can carry several
codes, and each route lists the codes it can answer with under each status.
A refusal is an expected answer. It means the request asked for something
that is not there, not yet approved, over a limit or not the key's to do,
and the code says which.

A request the API failed to handle for a reason of its own answers `500` with the plain-text body `Internal Server Error` rather than JSON. There is nothing to change in the request, and it can be retried later.

Every response names the request it answers in `X-Request-Id`: the id the request was sent with in that header, when it is well formed, else one the API gave it. Quote it when reporting a refusal or a failure: the API's log lines for that request carry it.

Before retrying a request that asked a printshop for something, such as
`POST /v1/prints/{id}/orders`, read what it was about first: the failure may
have come after the printshop took the order. Check the print's orders with
`GET /v1/orders?printId=<print id>` and an order's status with `GET /v1/orders/{id}`, and never
submit again while an order says `outcome_unknown`.

## A body that does not match its route

A body, query or path the route cannot accept is refused before the route
does anything, with a `422` or, on some routes, a `400`, whose `error` names
what was wrong. Some carry a field saying more, such as a one-line `reason`
or an `issues` list naming each field at fault. Each operation lists the codes
it can answer with.

## Refusals any route can answer

These come from checks that run before a route's own work: the key and its
origin, on the routes that take one, the rate limit and the body's size. They
are also listed in this document's `x-refusals`.

| Status | Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | The request carries no credential, or one that is unknown or revoked. |
| 401 | `member_link_required` | A connected store's integration key was sent to a route that acts as a member. The store links its user's Pixonaut account first (`POST /v1/connect/token` with `kind: "member_link"`) and sends the member key it is given. |
| 401 | `member_link_revoked` | A member key whose link no longer holds: it was revoked, its member left the workspace, or its store was disconnected. The store asks its user to link their account again. The store's own connection is not affected. |
| 403 | `origin_forbidden` | A publishable key was sent from an origin outside the key's allowlist. |
| 403 | `secret_key_required` | The route takes a secret key, and the request carried another credential. |
| 403 | `forbidden` | The route does not take the kind of credential sent. |
| 403 | `feature_disabled` | The tenant does not have the feature the key is for: `api` for a publishable or secret key, `mcp` for an MCP key. The key is kept, and is admitted again once the tenant has the feature. |
| 403 | `workspace_suspended` | The workspace the credential belongs to is suspended. Every credential of it is refused until the suspension is lifted; nothing of it is deleted. |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | Too many requests in the current window. Retry after the number of seconds in `retry-after`. |
| 422 | `payload_too_large` | The request body is larger than the route accepts. `maxBytes` is the limit. |
| 500 | `db_error` | The api could not read or write its database. |

## Rate limits

Each caller has a budget per bucket: an api key, a member, a person's MCP
keys together, or one visitor of a storefront's publishable key or share
link. All the visitors of one publishable key or link share a total, and all
of a workspace's callers share a ceiling, so one busy store leaves its
members room. The budgets are the same on every plan. A request past one is
refused with `429` and `rate_limited`, and the `retry-after` header says how
many seconds to wait; the windows slide, so the budget comes back gradually.

| Bucket | Counts | Window | One caller | A storefront key's or link's visitors together | The workspace together |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `proof` | Proofs: each one rendered | a minute | 30 | 90 | 150 |
| `validate` | Validating a design | a minute | 120 | 360 | 600 |
| `commit` | Committing a design | a minute | 30 | 90 | 150 |
| `pixel` | Pixel's turns | a minute | 20 | 60 | 100 |
| `pixelUpload` | Files attached to Pixel | a minute | 60 | 180 | 300 |
| `webhookPing` | Test requests to a webhook endpoint | a minute | 10 | 30 | 50 |
| `blankImport` | Importing blanks from a CSV, and its previews | a minute | 10 | 30 | 50 |
| `mcp` | MCP requests, per person across their MCP keys | a minute | 120 | 360 | 600 |

Public file addresses, hosted designer pages and share links are also
limited per visitor's address, and answer the same way.

## A studio session whose address is not verified

The studio's own session, signed in to an account whose email address is not
verified yet, is refused every write with `403` and `email_not_verified`,
whatever the route, except accepting an invitation, which verifies the
address. No key or integration meets it: the rule is about the signed-in
person.

get.description: The link a printshop is handed with an order, or the `fileUrl` a read of a completed print answers with. The token in the path is signed by the api and expires; no key is needed. Opening a read's link is a get of the print's files by its reader: the first counts as an order, and is refused as the print's own file route refuses one (`plan_limit_reached`, `order_balance_empty`, or `forbidden` for a reader without `orders:create`).

200.description: The print file: its PDF, or the raster its machine takes

limit.description: The limit the tenant is at: `templates`, `connectedStores`, `apiKeys`, `shareLinks`, `customDomains`, `printsMadePerMonth` (prints made without an order this month), `members`, `orders` (this month's orders, which getting a print's files without an order counts as), or a sandbox's own caps: `sandboxPrintsPerDay`, `sandboxPrintsPerMonth`, `sandboxOrdersPerMonth`. A sandbox shares every other limit with its live workspace. Always sent with `plan_limit_reached`.

max.description: How many the plan allows. Always sent with `plan_limit_reached`.

plan.description: The plan whose limit it is. Always sent with `plan_limit_reached`.

404.description: The token does not verify or has expired, or the print has no artwork

422.description: The order's machine lays a white or a varnish this print cannot be handed out with, or takes a raster this print is too large for

500.description: The request failed unexpectedly.

get.summary: Fetch a print's artwork

get.description: The links a custom printshop's delivery step hands the shop. The token in the path is signed by the api and expires; no key is needed. It names the print, the order it was made for, and whether it serves the print's file or that order's job ticket, which is read through the order.

schema.description: The job ticket of the order the link was made for: the print's ticket with that order's quantity

200.description: The print file, or its job ticket

404.description: The token does not verify or has expired, or the print has no such part

422.description: The order's machine lays a white or a varnish this print cannot be handed out with

500.description: The request failed unexpectedly.

get.summary: Fetch a print's file or ticket by delivery link

get.description: A font family's file by its content hash: a TTF for a renderer, a WOFF2 for a browser. Any cache may keep it for good, since the bytes at a hash never change. A TTF asked for with `text` is cut down to the glyphs those characters reach, every layout feature kept, so a renderer draws text made only of them as the whole face draws it; a `text` of more than 1000 distinct characters is served the whole face.

304.description: Not modified: the `If-None-Match` etag still holds

404.description: No font file by that name: `<sha256>.ttf` or `<sha256>.woff2` naming a hash the catalog has made (plain text)

copiedFrom.description: The blank this one was copied to its printshop from, or null.

blankId.description: The source blank's id, which may since have been deleted.

name.description: The source blank's name when it was copied.

deleted.description: When and by whom the blank was deleted, or null for a blank that is not. A deleted blank is read-only: restore it to change it.

at.description: When the blank was deleted, epoch ms.

by.description: The member who deleted it; null when a key did.

name.description: The member's name as it is now; null once unknown.

importFailure.description: The code a failed import failed with, such as `partner_failed` or `storage_quota_exceeded`; null unless `status` is `failed`.

options.description: The blank's options with their values, in the order the shopper sees them, a value no variant uses yet included. `axes` is their names.

oneOf.description: The value is drawn in one or two flat colours.

colours.description: One `#rrggbb` colour, or two for a heather or two-tone, drawn half and half.

tone.description: Whether a product in this value is light or dark, set by you. Absent, a colour fill's first colour decides (darker than mid grey is dark) and any other value is light. A template layer's on-dark value is used on a dark one.

oneOf.description: The value is drawn as a picture of it, such as a pattern.

assetId.description: An image in the workspace's asset library.

tone.description: Whether a product in this value is light or dark, set by you. Absent, a colour fill's first colour decides (darker than mid grey is dark) and any other value is light. A template layer's on-dark value is used on a dark one.

appearances.description: How each value looks to a shopper, by value: a colour fill, an image, or null for none. Every value of `values` is named.

localizedNames.description: The option's name per customer-facing language, by code: only the languages it has one in. A language left out reads `name`.

localizedValues.description: Each value's name per customer-facing language, by value: only the values that have one. A language left out reads the value itself.

tones.description: Whether a product in each value is light or dark, by value: the tone set on its appearance, else its colour fill's, else light. Every value of `values` is named. On a variant of a dark value a template's on-dark values are used.

optionsConfirmedAt.description: When the blank's options were confirmed: the merchant said it has one version, or added its first option. Null until then. A blank imported from a printshop's catalogue arrives confirmed.

order.description: The blank's stored views and the scenes it shows as one ordered list, each saying its source: `stock` (a scene), `catalogue` (the printshop's photos) or `own` (the merchant's). The first with a photo is the blank's picture. Answered for one blank, never in a list.

source.description: `catalogue` for the printshop's photos, `own` for the merchant's.

row.description: The option values the stock photo shows, by option name, of the options the blank's photos change with (`photosVaryBy`): shoppers see it only for the variants with these values. Absent or empty: every variant.

source.description: A scene from the library.

orderCount.description: How many orders name the blank, past ones included. Answered in a list, never for one blank, and only to a caller with `orders:read`.

paintBy.description: The option the blank's dyed photos are painted in, such as Colour: a stock photo that takes a dye, or a view drawn from a 3D render, shows each variant in its value's colour. null: the merchant's own photos are not painted and show as photographed, while a stock photo that takes a dye is painted in the first option with colours.

photoCoverage.description: How much of the blank is photographed. Answered in a list.

cells.description: The blank's rows (each combination of the values of the options its photos change with; one for All) times its views.

filled.description: The cells with a photo, of their own row or a covering one.

photosVaryBy.description: The options the blank's photos change with, in option order: each photo belongs to one row, its values of these, and shows every variant with them. Empty is All: one photo per view shows every variant.

placements.description: The blank's placements: the areas a design is printed into. An update replaces the whole list, so send every placement to keep.

areas.description: The placement's print area per row of the blank's `areasVaryBy` options, such as one per size; omitted or empty, the placement has one print area, its own. maxWidthMm and maxHeightMm are then the widest and tallest row, which every row fits inside.

bleedMm.description: Bleed past the trim on the row, in millimetres, 0 to 50. Omitted, the placement's.

dpi.description: Print resolution on the row in dots per inch. Omitted, the placement's.

foldMm.description: How far in from the trim the product folds on the row, in millimetres. Omitted, the placement's.

heightMm.description: The tallest print the row takes, in millimetres.

row.description: The row: a value for each `areasVaryBy` option, by option name. One area per row per placement.

safeAreaMm.description: Safe area inside the trim on the row, in millimetres, 0 to 50. Omitted, the placement's.

usualHeightMm.description: The height a print gets on the row when none is chosen, in millimetres, at most heightMm.

usualWidthMm.description: The width a print gets on the row when none is chosen, in millimetres, at most widthMm.

widthMm.description: The widest print the row takes, in millimetres.

bleedMm.description: Bleed past the trim on each side, in millimetres, 0 to 50. Omitted, its category's, else the workspace's.

coverage.description: How a print covers the placement: `within`, a print of any size up to the maximum placed inside it, or `full`, a print that is the whole area, such as an all-over-print panel. Omitted, `within`. A `full` placement's usual size is its area, and a request naming a smaller size is refused `print_size_not_area`.

defaultHeightMm.description: The height a print gets when none is chosen, in millimetres, at most maxHeightMm.

defaultWidthMm.description: The width a print gets when none is chosen, in millimetres, at most maxWidthMm.

dpi.description: Print resolution in dots per inch. Omitted, its category's, else 300.

fillColour.description: The `#rrggbb` colour an optional placement left undesigned is printed or delivered as. Null or omitted for none.

foldMm.description: How far in from the trim the product folds on every side, in millimetres, such as a canvas's wrap round its frame; the designer draws fold lines there. Omitted, no fold.

garments.description: Where the placement sits on each product the blank's stock photos show, one record per stock item for every scene of it: the stock item, a garment area of it, and the print's top left and width on it in millimetres. A placement with no record on a scene's stock item draws nothing on that scene. Refused with `placement_garment_area_unknown` when the stock item or the area is unknown, and `placement_garment_outside_area` when it reaches past the area.

area.description: The key of a garment area of the record's stock item.

stockItem.description: The stock item the record is on, by its key.

widthMm.description: The print's width on the product, in mm. Its height follows from the placement's print area ratio.

xMm.description: The print's left edge, in mm from the area's left.

yMm.description: The print's top edge, in mm from the area's top.

id.description: Unique within the blank; a short stable one such as `front`, which a template refers to it by.

linkWith.description: The placement it is linked with by default, such as a right sleeve with the left one: one design then drives both unless a designer link, an SDK mount or a design says otherwise. Null or omitted for none. A placement linked with one no longer on the blank is linked with none.

mirror.description: Whether this placement's print is mirrored left to right when the two are linked.

placementId.description: The id of the blank's other placement it is linked with by default.

maxHeightMm.description: The tallest print the placement takes, in millimetres.

maxWidthMm.description: The widest print the placement takes, in millimetres.

name.description: What it is called, such as Front or Back.

printMethod.description: How this placement is printed, such as dtg or screen. Omitted, its category's.

required.description: Whether an order on the blank must print it: one without a print for it is refused `placement_unfilled`. Omitted is false; a blank bound to its printshop's product takes it from the printshop.

safeAreaMm.description: Safe area inside the trim on each side, in millimetres, 0 to 50. Omitted, its category's, else the workspace's.

shape.description: Where on the product a print may go when that is not the whole rectangle: nothing is printed outside the outline or in a cut-out. Null or omitted, the whole rectangle.

cutByPrintShop.description: True when the print shop cuts the product to this shape: the outline and the cut-outs go into the print file as its cut line. Omitted, the product already has the shape.

dFrac.description: The shape as SVG path data in fractions of the print area, 0 to 1 across and down (curves, no arcs): its first subpath the outline, every further one a cut-out, filled even-odd, each subpath closed.

shopName.description: Printed as: the name the blank's printshop knows the placement by, on orders and job sheets. Null or omitted prints the placement's name.

views.description: The ways the placement is photographed, such as Flat or On model. Every photo of one view shares its pixel size and its print area.

fromPrintshop.description: True on a view a blank bound to its printshop's product took from the printshop (its import, Add colours, model photos): its photo size and print area are the printshop's and cannot change by hand. Absent on a view the workspace added. Set only by the printshop's own paths; a save that sends it is ignored.

id.description: Unique within the blank.

label.description: What it is called, such as Flat or On model; unique among its placement's views of its kind, the printshop's or the merchant's, ignoring case.

localizedLabels.description: What it is called per customer-facing language, by code: only the languages it has a name in; a language left out reads `label`. No two views of its placement and kind read the same in one language, ignoring case.

maskAssetId.description: A library asset of the view's photo size: where it is light the print shows, where it is dark the print is hidden, as behind a sleeve or a fold. Absent hides nothing.

mesh.description: Control points the print is laid through or, marked cut, cut to, rows from its top edge and points from its left, as [x, y] in the photo's original pixels; at least 2 and at most 33 along each side. Absent, the print is laid in the rect.

cut.description: The points draw a shape to cut the print to (CONTEXT.md → Region cut) rather than a mesh to bend it through: the print is laid flat over the box the points span, at its own proportions and filling it, and everything outside the shape the outer points draw is cut away. Absent, the print is warped through the mesh.

points.description: The rows of control points, from the print's top edge.

items.description: One row of control points, from the print's left edge.
One control point, [x, y] in the photo's original pixels.

partnerStyleKey.description: The printshop's own key for the photo style the view was made from, such as a model or lifestyle style; absent on a view made by hand or imported with the product.

photoSizePx.description: The pixel size every photo of the view has; null until the view holds a photo.

photos.description: The view's product photos, each the same size as the view.

assetId.description: The photo's asset id, as the assets feature returns it after an upload.

displacementStrength.description: How far the photo's folds move the design, more than 0 and at most 1. null moves nothing. Omitted, its category's, else nothing.

id.description: The photo's id, unique within the blank: the `mockupId` a render and a mockup link name.

row.description: The photo's value of each `photosVaryBy` option; empty when there are none. One photo per row per view.

shadingStrength.description: How strongly the photo's light and shade carry onto the design, 0 (none) to 1 (all). Omitted, its category's, else the default strength.

textureStrength.description: How strongly the photo's fine detail, such as a weave or a grain, shows through the print, 0 (none) to 1 (all). Omitted, its category's, else, as for null, the default strength.

variantRefs.description: The variants the photo shows, from its `row`. A write may name the row by these instead.

warp.description: How the design wraps round the product. null lies it flat. Omitted, its category's, else flat.

curvature.description: How far round the product the design wraps, more than 0 and at most 1. Flat is a null warp, not 0.

edgeFalloff.description: How much the design darkens toward the product's sides, 0 (none) to 1 (black at the edge). Omitted, none.

kind.description: The kind of wrap; `cylinder` is the only one.

piece.description: A pattern piece of the view's UV pass, 1 to 254: the region's print is read through the pixels the pass marks with it, in place of a mesh.

placementRectPx.description: Where the print area sits on every photo of the view, in the original photo's pixels; null until it is marked.

h.description: The print area's height, in pixels.

w.description: The print area's width, in pixels.

x.description: The print area's left edge, in pixels from the photo's left.

y.description: The print area's top edge, in pixels from the photo's top.

position.description: The view's place in the blank's one list of views and scenes, from 0. The first with a photo is the blank's picture. Read only.

printWindowMm.description: The part of the region's piece its print covers, in millimetres on the piece's unwrapped surface from its top-left corner, such as a square on the side of a cup: the print is read inside it, at the window's size, and the product shows plain outside it. It lies inside its piece, and needs the piece's size on the view. Absent, the print covers the whole piece.

widthMm.description: The window's width, in mm.

xMm.description: The window's left edge, in mm from the piece's left.

yMm.description: The window's top edge, in mm from the piece's top.

sceneId.description: The scene this view shows. A scene's view is built from the blank's chosen scenes and is read only.

scenePosition.description: On a scene's view, its `position`, for a reader that orders scenes by it.

source.description: Where the view's photos come from: `stock` (a scene from the library), `catalogue` (the printshop's) or `own` (the merchant's). Read only.

sourceWindowMm.description: The piece of the placement's print the region shows, in millimetres from the print's top-left corner, such as a roll's window; clamped to the print when the print is smaller. Absent, the region shows the whole print at the size of the render's variant.

widthMm.description: The window's width, in mm.

xMm.description: The window's left edge, in mm from the print's left.

yMm.description: The window's top edge, in mm from the print's top.

takesDye.description: On a scene's view, whether a variant's colour recolours it. One that takes none shows only the variants of its colour.

uvPasses.description: The maps the view was rendered with from a 3D model of the product, each the view's photo size; a region naming a piece is drawn through them. Absent, the view's regions are laid in their rect or mesh.

multiplyAssetId.description: The multiply pass: the garment's shadows and folds.

occluderAssetId.description: What lies in front of the print, drawn over it: hands, cords and hair. A scene's alone, and read only.

pieceSizesMm.description: Each piece's print size on the model, as its `view.json` gives it: what a region's print window is placed on. Absent, no region of the view may name a print window.

items.description: A piece of the UV pass and its print's size on the model.

heightMm.description: The piece's print height on the model, in mm.

widthMm.description: The piece's print width on the model, in mm.

zoomTier.description: On a scene's view read at its preview tier, its files at the zoom tier.

maxHeightMm.description: The tallest print the placement takes, in millimetres.

maxWidthMm.description: The widest print the placement takes, in millimetres.

name.description: What it is called, such as Front or Back.

printMethod.description: How this placement is printed, such as dtg or screen. Omitted, its category's.

required.description: Whether an order on the blank must print it: one without a print for it is refused `placement_unfilled`. Omitted is false; a blank bound to its printshop's product takes it from the printshop.

safeAreaMm.description: Safe area inside the trim on each side, in millimetres, 0 to 50. Omitted, its category's, else the workspace's.

shape.description: Where on the product a print may go when that is not the whole rectangle: nothing is printed outside the outline or in a cut-out. Null or omitted, the whole rectangle.

cutByPrintShop.description: True when the print shop cuts the product to this shape: the outline and the cut-outs go into the print file as its cut line. Omitted, the product already has the shape.

dFrac.description: The shape as SVG path data in fractions of the print area, 0 to 1 across and down (curves, no arcs): its first subpath the outline, every further one a cut-out, filled even-odd, each subpath closed.

shopName.description: Printed as: the name the blank's printshop knows the placement by, on orders and job sheets. Null or omitted prints the placement's name.

views.description: The ways the placement is photographed, such as Flat or On model. Every photo of one view shares its pixel size and its print area.

fromPrintshop.description: True on a view a blank bound to its printshop's product took from the printshop (its import, Add colours, model photos): its photo size and print area are the printshop's and cannot change by hand. id.description: Unique within the blank.

label.description: What it is called, such as Flat or On model; unique among its placement's views of its kind, the printshop's or the merchant's, ignoring case.

localizedLabels.description: What it is called per customer-facing language, by code: only the languages it has a name in; a language left out reads `label`. No two views of its placement and kind read the same in one language, ignoring case.

maskAssetId.description: A library asset of the view's photo size: where it is light the print shows, where it is dark the print is hidden, as behind a sleeve or a fold. Absent hides nothing.

mesh.description: Control points the print is laid through or, marked cut, cut to, rows from its top edge and points from its left, as [x, y] in the photo's original pixels; at least 2 and at most 33 along each side. Absent, the print is laid in the rect.

cut.description: The points draw a shape to cut the print to (CONTEXT.md → Region cut) rather than a mesh to bend it through: the print is laid flat over the box the points span, at its own proportions and filling it, and everything outside the shape the outer points draw is cut away. get.description: The placement and mockup ids a mockup render names, each placement's views with their labels, photo sizes and print rects, and each view's photos (the mockups) with the variants each shows, in stored order. The order is not an identifier: it changes when the blank is reordered in the studio, so persist the ids. A placement whose stored sizes are unusable is left out. Each placement carries the largest and default print box, whether a print covers its whole area, the bleed and safe area it prints with (its own, else the tenant's default) and its print method. Each mockup carries a `thumbnailUrl`, a link to its photo that opens with no key for an hour or two, and a `mount`: what a storefront passes to the designer as one of `mockups`, with a photo link that stays valid for at least 30 days. With `lang`, each view's label is the blank's for it in that language, else its own.

parameters.description: The language the blank's options, their values and its views are named in, one of `en`, `sv`, `de`, `fr`, `es`, `nl`, `da`, `nb`, `fi`: each name the blank has in it, else its own. Absent, every name is its own.

patch.description: Called with the store's own integration key. `additionalOrigins` is for a store whose pages also run on other hosts of its own domain: its counterpart with or without `www.`, a checkout or a headless storefront. It sets the origins the publishable key takes besides the site's own, which then admit the designer with that key and may receive a designer link's `returnUrl`. An origin on any other domain is `400 invalid_origin`, naming it, and nothing changes; a member mints a publishable key for it in the studio. More origins than the limit is `400 too_many_origins`. Reconnecting starts again from the site's own origin. `brandId` sets the brand the store's hosted pages are drawn in: proof pages, correction links and designer links its key creates from then on, each keeping the brand it was created in. An id that is not one of the workspace's brands is `404 brand_not_found`, and nothing changes. A member may set it in the studio too; a brand a store is drawn in cannot be deleted. `printFileForm` sets the form print files of designs the store sends are made in, and `printFileTextTolerance` how far their live text may lie from its outline, each unless their template chooses otherwise; null follows the workspace's setting.

A request stays current until a member turns the switch off or asks again, it is turned off in WordPress, the store disconnects or a handover names none; being answered does not end it, so a retry may bring a new secret, which replaces the one held. Naming any other request is `409 store_access_request_stale` and changes nothing: revoke that credential and do not retry. Naming none always wins. post.description: Called by the store's server with the code the studio sent its merchant back with, the PKCE verifier it made the challenge from, and the same `redirect_uri`. Answers, once, an integration key, a publishable key bound to the store's origin, a webhook endpoint registered at the store with its signing secret, and the member key of the member who approved. A code works once, for a minute: any attempt uses it, and every refusal is `invalid_grant`, after which the store connects again. Connecting a site that is already connected replaces its connection, revoking what it was given before. With `kind: "member_link"` and the store's integration key as the bearer, exchanges a member link's code for the approving member's member key instead; a code approved for another store or workspace is `invalid_grant`.

One live standing design per template version, blank, placement and size: the same request again answers the same design, 200 with `created: false`, and two sent at once make one. A rejected or deleted standing design is not found, and the next request makes another. `blankId` and `placementId`, both or neither, and `widthMm` and `heightMm`, both or neither, as on `POST /v1/designs`: no size is the placement's default size, which finds the design naming that size made. deletable.description: Whether `DELETE /v1/designs/{id}` would take the design now: it is not approved, and no print of it exists, of any revision and in any status.

garmentTone.description: The tone the design was drawn for: `dark` on a variant whose colour is dark, where each layer's on-dark value is used; `light` otherwise. A correction judges its values against the template as that tone draws it.

hasPrint.description: Whether the design's current text has been printed. A correction leaves that print showing the old text; it is never ordered, and the corrected design is printed again only when someone prints it once it is approved.

language.description: The language the design was made in, one of `en`, `sv`, `de`, `fr`, `es`, `nl`, `da`, `nb`, `fi`: its template was read in it, with that language's overrides, and its document and print file are that language's.

origin.description: Where the design came from: the door it was committed through. A duplicate's is whoever duplicated it.

personalDataErasedAt.description: When the design's own personal data was erased (`POST /v1/designs/{id}/erase-personal-data`), or null. An erased design's document holds none of the text or pictures its customer put in, and nothing more is printed, ordered or corrected from it.

pictureUrl.description: A link to a drawing of the design's current revision, as `GET /v1/designs/{id}/revisions/{revision}/image` draws it, that opens with no key for an hour or two. It opens that revision alone, and stops opening once the design's personal data is erased. Null once it was.

placementId.description: The placement on the blank this design was fitted to when it was made; null whenever `blankId` is. Kept while the blank is, so it may name a placement since removed from the blank: the print box frozen into the document is what prints.

previewOpened.description: Whether the customer saw the proof before approving. `true` when they approved on a deciding proof page, which showed them that revision's proof, whatever the commit said, and when they approved in a hosted designer and the commit said nothing. On an approval by a store's key or with consent, what the caller committing it said, from the SDK's `wasPreviewOpened()`. `null` means this does not apply: a review time ran out, or a member or an automation approved it with no consent, so no customer approved, short of what a hosted designer's customer already answered. widthMm.description: The print's trim width, in millimetres.

proofVariant.description: The variant of the blank the customer previewed the design's proof on, by ref, as `POST /v1/proofs` was sent it; null when it named none. For display only: an order names its own variant.

proofViewId.description: The view of the blank's placement the customer previewed the design's proof in, by id, as `POST /v1/proofs` was sent it; null when it named none.

rejectionReason.description: Why the design was rejected, as its rejection said (`reason` on `POST /v1/designs/{id}/reject`); null when it is not rejected, or was rejected without one. Its customer is shown it on the proof page.

shareLinkId.description: The share link whose page made the design: committed there, or from a proof it made. Null when no link made it.

templateVersion.description: The version of the template the design was made from: `templateId` after its `@`. A design committed from a proof token was made from the proof's version, whatever the template's latest is now.

variantRow.description: The size the design was made for, on a blank whose print areas change with its size: the blank's option values it was sized at, such as `{"Size": "XL"}`. patch.description: Applies `values` on top of the design's document under the rules its template version sets, keeps the size it was committed at, and sends it back to awaiting approval: any approval, made or scheduled, is cleared, and nothing is printed or ordered until it is approved again. Renders a proof of the corrected document, which becomes the design's proof (`proofId`); a correction whose proof cannot be rendered is refused, and writes nothing. Or, with `proofToken` instead, makes a correction proof's document the design's next revision and that proof the design's proof, refused `proof_not_for_design` for a proof of another design, or of no design, `proof_adjusts_layout` for a layout adjustment's proof, which `POST /v1/designs/standing` takes, and `revision_changed` once the design has moved past the revision the proof was made from. Emits `design.edited`. A correction that leaves the document as it is writes nothing — not a revision, not a cleared approval, not an event — and answers `edited: false`. Refused once any print of the design has an order.

post.description: A stateless JSON-RPC MCP server (protocol versions `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18` and `2025-03-26`) over POST alone: `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call` and `notifications/cancelled`. A connected store's member key acts as the member its user linked, exactly as an MCP key acts as the member who minted it: `tools/list` is the tools that member's MCP key would get, and each `tools/call` runs the tool's route as the member, judged by their grants, the workspace's features and its plan. A tool the member may not use answers `result.isError: true` with the route's reason; an unknown tool is JSON-RPC error `-32602`. There are no confirm cards: a destructive tool says so in `annotations.destructiveHint`, and a template change that needs an author's confirmation is refused in `isError`. The workspace must have `mcp`. The store's own integration key is refused `member_link_required`.

post.description: A secret key, an integration key, or a studio member holding `orders:create`. Places ONE order for every print in `prints`: the prints of one physical item, a front and a back of one shirt, made by one printshop as one item. The prints must be prints of designs committed on the same blank, each in a placement of its own, or all on no blank, completed or still rendering. An order of prints still rendering is written `awaiting_prints` and answered 201 at once; it goes to its printshop on its own once every print is complete, checked then against what needs the files (`technique_not_offered`, the sizes, the printshop's required keys), and a refusal then leaves it `failed` with `failureKind` naming it. A print of it that fails fails it `print_failed`, and prints not complete within three hours of placing fail it `prints_timed_out`. A print that failed is refused `409 print_not_completed`. `designs` names approved designs in place of their prints: the order makes a new print of each, as `POST /v1/prints` would, and waits for them, except that a standing design's order reuses the print of its current revision, completed or still rendering, and makes one only when there is none or it failed; an unknown design is `404 design_not_found`, one not approved `409 design_not_approved`, and nothing is written. Naming both `prints` and `designs`, or neither, is `400`. Every check that needs no files runs at placement: `422 print_without_placement` names a print committed before its placement was recorded, `422 mixed_blanks` answers prints on different blanks or some on a blank and some on none, and `422 duplicate_placement` two in one placement. Prints on a blank go to their blank's printshop, set when the blank was created; every print is checked against that printshop. `printshopId` naming another printshop is refused `422 printshop_differs_from_blank`, and naming the blank's own as an unknown field. Prints on no blank, such as a sign's front and back, go to the printshop the first print's design was committed with, else `printshopId`, else the workspace default, else are refused `409 print_needs_printshop`, except in a sandbox, where the order is placed with no printshop (`printshopConnectionId` null, `adapter` `none`); a print whose design was committed with another printshop is refused `422 print_committed_elsewhere`, naming it. A printshop that cannot make several prints as one item answers `422 printshop_cannot_combine`, and prints whose designs disagree on what the printshop makes one item from answer `422 prints_disagree` naming the key: nothing is written either way. One print places exactly the order `POST /v1/prints/{id}/orders` would. `quantity`, `externalRef`, `recipient`, `shippingAddress` and the `Idempotency-Key` header are as there; the first print's design's captured delivery is the one the order takes when the body names neither a recipient nor an address. A partner refusing the order is still a 201: the order is recorded as `failed`. A printshop the merchant paused takes no order: one going there is refused `409 printshop_paused`, naming it, and nothing is written. A print made by a method its printshop does not print with, where the printshop states what it prints with, is refused `422 technique_not_offered`, naming the placement, the method and the printshop's, and nothing is written. A placement its blank says an order must print, left without a print, is refused `422 placement_unfilled`, naming it, and nothing is written. A design has one live order, in any status but `failed` and `cancelled`, whoever placed it: an order of prints of a design that has one, or naming such a design, is refused `409 design_already_ordered`, naming the design and its newest live order, and nothing is written; two sent at once place one. `reorder: true` orders it again on purpose. A standing design is never refused `design_already_ordered`: it is ordered on every sale. A repeat with the first request's `Idempotency-Key` is answered with the first order before this is asked.

parameters.description: Your own key for this request. A repeat with the same key and body within 24 hours is answered with what the first one made, marked `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and makes nothing; the same key with another body is refused `idempotency_key_reused`, and a repeat while the first is still being answered `idempotency_key_in_use`. A request that is refused makes nothing, so its key may be sent again.

A request that is refused makes nothing, so its key may be sent again.

designs.description: The designs of one item in place of its prints, each an approved design of one side, committed on the same blank in a placement of its own; the first is the order's lead. The order makes a new print of each, as `POST /v1/prints` would, and waits for them; a standing design's order reuses the print of its current revision, completed or still rendering, and makes one only when there is none or it failed. Name `prints` or `designs`, not both.

prints.description: The prints of one item, each a print of a design committed on the same blank in a placement of its own, completed or still rendering; the first is the order's lead, which `printId` names on the order. printshopId.description: The printshop to make this order, for a print with no blank whose design named none when it was committed. A print on a blank is made by the blank's printshop: naming another is refused with `printshop_differs_from_blank`, and naming the blank's own as an unknown field. Absent or `null`, a print with no blank goes to the printshop its design was committed with, else the tenant's default.

quantity.description: How many copies to order. A whole number of 1 or more; 1 when left out.

reorder.description: Order the design again on purpose. A design has one live order (in any status but `failed` and `cancelled`): absent or false, an order of a design that has one is refused `409 design_already_ordered`, naming the design and its newest live order, and nothing is written. True places the order whatever orders the design has.

patch.description:
A secret key moves an order forward by hand, for a printshop with no API of its own such as the local one: printed, shipped (optionally with `tracking`) or failed (optionally with a `reason`). An order moves forward only, never out of shipped, failed or cancelled, and never to cancelled, which only `POST /v1/orders/{id}/cancel` reaches by asking its printshop.

An order whose submission's answer was lost is `outcome_unknown`. Once you have asked its printshop, settle it: `failed` when the printshop does not have it, after which `POST /v1/orders/{id}/retry` submits it again, or `submitted` when it does, optionally with `externalOrderRef`, the printshop's own reference for it, so its status is followed from then on. A connected store's integration key and a studio member holding `orders:update` may make these two moves and no other. Settling needs a `reason`, kept in the audit log with who settled it; refused `422 order_status_reason_required` without one. A reference another order holds, or one other than the order's own, is refused `409 order_reference_taken`.

In a sandbox, whose orders reach no printshop, an integration key and a member move an order as a secret key does, so a store can rehearse an order shipping or failing.

A `reason` with any status but `failed` is kept in the audit log only. Any other move is refused `409 order_status_not_allowed`.

post.description: A secret key, or a connected store's integration key or a studio member holding `orders:update`. Asks the order's printshop to stop it, and moves it to `cancelled`, a final status, only once the printshop says it did: `order.cancelled` is emitted. An order in `held`, `awaiting_prints`, `submitted`, `queued`, `outcome_unknown` can be asked about; one already cancelled is answered unchanged. An order still waiting for its prints (`awaiting_prints`) is cancelled at once, without asking a printshop, which has not been handed it. An order left at its printshop is refused `409 order_at_printshop`, whose `cause` says why: `made` (printed or shipped), `begun` (the printshop has begun it and did not cancel it), `cannot_cancel` (its printshop cannot stop orders), `not_connected` (its printshop is no longer connected), or `status_moved` (the printshop cancelled it, but it shipped meanwhile). Ask the printshop. A failed order is refused `409 order_status_not_allowed`, and one whose submission has not been answered yet `409 order_in_flight`. A printshop that could not be reached is `503 cancel_unavailable`, and the order stands; `retryable` says whether asking again may work. Refunds are your store's: cancelling an order moves no money.

patch.description:
A secret key, a connected store's integration key, or a studio member holding `orders:update`. Gives an order its `recipient` and `shippingAddress` after it was sent: one placed without them, or one whose customer moved. Both are checked as `POST /v1/orders` checks them, and an address without the postcode its printshop needs is refused `422 postal_code_required`.

The order's printshop is told, and the order's `delivery` says what it made of it: `accepted`, `refused` (in its own `words`; the order keeps the address the printshop has), `sending` while it is being told, or `carried` when what the printshop had not been sent yet takes the new address, so nothing extra is sent. A printshop that takes no address changes is refused `409 address_change_not_accepted`, naming it: a custom printshop takes them when its `acceptsAddressUpdates` is on, and an integration when it can tell its partner. An order that has shipped, failed, been cancelled or had its personal data erased, whose outcome is unknown, whose submission has not been answered yet, or that its printshop is already making is refused `409 order_past_address_change`, naming its status. A printshop that could not be told is `503 address_change_unavailable`, and nothing changed.

Each change emits `order.delivery_changed`, again when a change that was `sending` is answered; neither carries the address. Send an `Idempotency-Key` to make a retried request safe.

parameters.description: Your own key for this request. A repeat with the same key and body within 24 hours is answered with what the first one made, marked `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and makes nothing; the same key with another body is refused `idempotency_key_reused`, and a repeat while the first is still being answered `idempotency_key_in_use`. A request that is refused makes nothing, so its key may be sent again.

post.description: A secret key, or a connected store's integration key or a studio member holding `orders:update`. Erases the order's `recipient` and `shippingAddress`, what a custom printshop's delivery steps were rendered with, and every stored reason the order failed (its `lastError`, its history's and its notifications'), which may repeat them; a step not yet sent is closed as failed. The order itself stays, with its print, status, history, quantity and `externalRef`, which is your own reference and is not erased. `personalDataErasedAt` says when. Refused `409 order_in_flight` until the order has shipped, failed or been cancelled, since its printshop may still need the address. Erasing an order already erased answers it unchanged. An erasure cannot be undone, and does not reach what the printshop was already sent.

patch.description:
The order marked printed, shipped (optionally with tracking) or failed (optionally with a reason), by the same rules as `PATCH /v1/orders/{id}`, and answered as its job. A printshop link gives a reason with failed only; a secret key may give one with any status, and must to settle an order whose outcome is unknown. A printshop link sending shipped with tracking for an order already shipped corrects its tracking: the order stays shipped, and `order.tracking_changed` (`order.tracking_added` for an order shipped without any) tells the store.

A member holding `orders:update` reports for a printshop a person works, one that takes its orders as delivery steps, as its link does: printed, shipped or failed, a reason with failed only, never out of an unknown outcome. The move is audited as theirs. An order to a printshop whose API reports on it is refused `409 order_status_not_allowed`; in a sandbox a member moves an order as `PATCH /v1/orders/{id}` lets them. An MCP key is answered the job without its tickets, which carry who the order is for and where it ships.

get.description: A secret key, or a connected store's integration key or a studio member holding `orders:create`. Every blank of the workspace but the order's own, at any printshop, for `POST /v1/orders/{id}/retry` with `reroute`: those the order's prints fit first, then the rest, each half by name, 50 to a page with the total. A print fits a placement whose largest print holds its trim size, width against width and height against height, and is that size where the placement is printed across its whole area, and whose print method is the one it was made by; it goes to the placement of its own placement's name when the blank has one. A fitting blank lists each print's placements; another says why, per print (`print_exceeds_placement` with both sizes, `print_short_of_area` with the print's size and the area of a placement printed across its whole area, `technique_differs` with both methods, `technique_unknown`, `no_placement_fits`), or `too_few_placements` when they cannot take one print each. post.description: Places a new order for the same print as a failed one, recording which order it replaces. A print of it that failed is rendered again in place, under the same id and from the design revision it was made from, and the new order is `awaiting_prints` until its prints complete, then goes to its printshop on its own; a render that fails again fails it `print_failed`, and it may be retried again. A print of it still rendering is waited for in the same way. It goes to the printshop the failed order went to, which is its blank's: a blank's printshop is set when the blank is created. A body naming a printshop is refused as unknown. With `reroute`, the order goes to another blank and its printshop instead, the failed order's printshop is not called, and no blank moves; it is refused 422 when that blank is unknown or the failed order's, when a print is left without a placement or two share one, when a print goes elsewhere than the placement of its own name, and when a print does not fit its placement (`print_exceeds_placement`, `print_short_of_area`, `technique_differs`, `technique_unknown`). A print on no blank was made by no method and takes its placement's, unless that placement is embroidered. Refused when the order is not `failed`, reached the printshop, or has already been submitted again; A failed order with `failureKind` `missing_fulfilment_keys` or `blank_needed`, of prints on no blank, goes where it would go now rather than back. Refused 422, writing nothing, when the printshop it would go to cannot take it or the design lacks a key that printshop requires, 409 `printshop_paused` when that printshop is paused, and 422 `technique_not_offered` when it does not print with the print's method, and 422 `placement_unfilled` when a placement the blank must print has no print.

reroute.description: Sends the order to another blank rather than back to its own: the same prints, copies, reference and address, at that blank's printshop. The prints are not made again, so each must fit the placement it goes to: its trim size within the placement's largest print, never turned, and made by the placement's print method. `GET /v1/orders/{id}/reroute-targets` lists the blanks it fits.

With `Prefer: wait` it answers once the print has rendered, `201` with its job ticket, or `render_failed`. A studio member or a connected store's integration key needs `prints:create`.

A request that is refused makes nothing, so its key may be sent again.
