post.description: A secret key, or a connected store's integration key or a studio member holding `orders:create`. Places an order for a print with its blank's printshop, set when the blank was created. A print still rendering is waited for: the order is written `awaiting_prints` and goes to its printshop on its own once the print is complete, as `POST /v1/orders` describes; a print that failed is refused `409 print_not_completed`. A print with no blank goes to the printshop its design was committed with, else the one `printshopId` names, else the tenant's default, and is refused `409 print_needs_printshop` with none; in a sandbox it is placed with no printshop instead (`printshopConnectionId` null, `adapter` `none`). The order records which. For a print on a blank, `printshopId` naming another printshop is refused `422 printshop_differs_from_blank`, and naming the blank's own as an unknown field. A printshop named here that cannot take the order (unknown, disconnected, or unavailable because its integration is no longer registered) is a 422 and no order is written, as is a design whose fulfilment payload lacks a key that printshop requires. A connected store's integration key is answered 201 instead of that key's refusal, and of a design on no blank at a printshop that needs a blank: its customer has paid, so the order is written `failed`, with `failureKind` `missing_fulfilment_keys` or `blank_needed`, for a member to send to a blank. `quantity` is how many copies this order wants, 1 when the body leaves it out; the same print can be ordered again with another, with `reorder: true`. A design has one live order, in any status but `failed` and `cancelled`, whoever placed it: an order of a print of a design that has one is refused `409 design_already_ordered`, naming the design and its newest live order, and nothing is written; two sent at once place one. A standing design is never refused `design_already_ordered`: its print is ordered on every sale. A repeat with the first request's `Idempotency-Key` is answered with the first order before this is asked, and a replacement of a failed order needs no `reorder`. `externalRef` is your own reference for the order (your order or line id; not unique, and `GET /v1/orders?externalRef=` finds it), and `recipient` and `shippingAddress` say who it is for and where it ships; all three are optional, reach the printshop on the job ticket, and are never written to logs. The design's first order takes the recipient and address its customer gave on its address capture page (`PUT /v1/designs/{id}/delivery`) when this body names neither; a body naming either is used alone, and the customer's answer is dropped. A partner refusing the order, or a printshop that has been disconnected, is still a 201: the order is recorded as `failed`, naming it and why (`printshop_disconnected`). A printshop the merchant paused takes no order: one going there is refused `409 printshop_paused`, naming it, and nothing is written. A print made by a method its printshop does not print with, where the printshop states what it prints with, is refused `422 technique_not_offered`, naming the placement, the method and the printshop's, and nothing is written. A placement its blank says an order must print, left without a print, is refused `422 placement_unfilled`, naming it, and nothing is written. With `replacesOrderId`, the order replaces a failed order of this print, as `POST /v1/orders/{id}/retry` would but with what this body asks for, and is refused as a retry is.

parameters.description: Your own key for this request. A repeat with the same key and body within 24 hours is answered with what the first one made, marked `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and makes nothing; the same key with another body is refused `idempotency_key_reused`, and a repeat while the first is still being answered `idempotency_key_in_use`. A request that is refused makes nothing, so its key may be sent again.

post.description: Opens one hosted page about one template, design or order to whoever holds the link. Answers with the token, which is never shown again. A member may hand out only what they hold themselves; a printshop page takes `printshops:update`, an address capture page `orders:create`. A connected store's integration key hands out what its grants hold, such as a deciding proof page it emails its customer, who approves or rejects there; the page is drawn in the brand named by `brandId`, or the workspace's default.

brandId.description: The brand the link's page is drawn in: its name, logo and accent colour (`GET /v1/brands`). Refused `brand_not_found` unless it is one of the workspace's. Absent, a link a connected store's key hands out keeps the store's brand, and any other is drawn in whichever brand is the workspace's default when it opens. A brand a link that still opens names cannot be deleted.

period.description: `total` counts every design the link made; `hour`, `day` and `week` the last 60 minutes, 24 hours or 7 days, rolling.

kind.description: The page the link opens. A correction link is minted for its design by `POST /v1/designs/{id}/correction-links`.

locale.description: A proof page only: the language it is shown in, one of `en`, `sv`, `de`, `fr`, `es`, `nl`, `da`, `nb`, `fi`. Absent, the page is shown in the workspace's default language. The link's `url` carries `?lang=<locale>` when it names one. Refused `locale_not_allowed` for any other kind.

mayDecide.description: A proof page only: whether its holder may approve or reject the design. Handing that out takes `designs:update` as well as `designs:read`.

name.description: The workspace's own name for the link (`Spring market stand`), at most 80 characters, never shown on its page. Trimmed, inner spaces made one; empty is no name. Unique among the workspace's working links, case aside: one another holds is refused `share_link_name_taken` naming the holder, a longer one `share_link_name_too_long`. A withdrawn or expired link frees its name.

orderId.description: An address capture page only: the one order of the design its answer reads and changes, whatever orders of the design are placed later. Refused `order_not_found` unless it holds a print of the design (and, for a connected store, the store placed it), `order_closed` once it has shipped, will not be made or its personal data was erased, and `order_not_allowed` for any other kind. Absent, the page reads and changes the design's newest open order.

placementFrame.description: A designer only: whether its page draws the placement frame, the ring and corner handles around the shopper's picture, at rest, as the SDK's `showPlacementFrame` does. Refused `placement_frame_not_allowed` for any other kind. Absent, the frame shows only while the picture is dragged or sized on the preview.

printAreaFrame.description: A designer only: whether its page draws a thin frame around the print area on the product photo, as the SDK's `showPrintAreaFrame` does. Refused `print_area_frame_not_allowed` for any other kind. Absent, no frame.

returnUrl.description: A proof page only: where it sends the customer once they have asked for changes, with `state`, so the store can open the design for editing. Refused `return_url_not_allowed` for any other kind: a designer that returns to a store is minted by `POST /v1/templates/{id}/designer-links`, a correction page by `POST /v1/designs/{id}/correction-links`. On one of the origins the tenant's publishable keys are allowed on.

state.description: Carried back to `returnUrl` untouched, for the store to match the customer to its own session. Only with `returnUrl`.

subjectId.description: What the page is about: a template's base id for a designer, a design's id for a proof page or address capture, an order's id for an order status or printshop page.

post.description: With `ids`, withdraws up to 100 links and answers each `revoked` or `not_found`; a link the caller could not have handed out (to a connected store's integration key, one its store did not hand out) is `not_found`, as `DELETE /v1/share-links/{id}` answers it. With `createdByKeyId`, withdraws every working link that api key or connected store handed out and answers how many, without revoking the key, which may hand out new ones. Each link withdrawn is audited as a single withdrawal is.

results.description: One entry per id asked for, in order, each once.

outcome.description: `revoked`: the link no longer works. `not_found`: no working link of that id the caller may manage — unknown, already withdrawn, or not theirs.

revoked.description: How many of the key's working links were withdrawn.

delete.description: The link's page stops opening at once. Revoking one already revoked changes nothing. A link the caller could not have handed out (to a connected store's integration key, one its store did not hand out) is answered as not found.

patch.description: Changes a working link's name or, on a designer link, its design limit and anything it was handed out with, each change audited. The link keeps its id, token and address, so a store's product page need not change: a visit after the change opens on the new settings, and a design made before keeps what it was made with. A designer link takes every field `POST /v1/templates/{id}/designer-links` takes, judged as that route judges them, and `templateId` for the template it opens; what its page shows (the blank and placement, sizes, photos, views, variants, `sides`, `layout` and `linkedPlacements`) is sent whole, and any of it replaces all of it. It is held to the rules a new link is: a side for every placement its blank says an order must print (`422 placement_unfilled`, naming it), sizes its blank takes (`422 variant_row_invalid`), a panel layout its blank has (`422 unknown_layout`), that still fits the blank at the size the link sells (`409 layout_out_of_date`) and whose canvas is the template's shape (`422 layout_wrong_ratio`), and linked sides that print one template (`422 linked_templates_differ`); its linked groups are kept as a new link keeps them, from its setting or what its blank suggests. Every other field absent is left as it is, and null removes it. Any of them on another kind is refused `designer_settings_not_allowed`. A name another working link holds is refused `share_link_name_taken`; a withdrawn or expired link, or one the caller could not have handed out (to a connected store's integration key, one its store did not hand out), is answered as not found. Nothing is changed when any part is refused.

get.description: The whole published document, which the designer validates and lays out against, and the form generated from it. Every field of `formSchema` has a `label` a customer can read, never a prop name: the author's, in `lang`, or the form's own word for what the field sets, in `lang`, else in the workspace's default language, with `labelIsDefault` true, so a server prints what the designer draws. `optionLabels` holds the tenant's own words for the options the template offers, when it has named any: each shape's, die's or picture's name for `lang`, else for the workspace's default language, else its own name; `dieShapeId` names the die-cut the author chose, `layerShapeIds` the shape each customer-editable shape layer starts on, by layer id, and `offeredShapes` holds the outline of every shape a customer may pick, for the die-cut or a shape layer. `printMargins` is the reading tenant's default bleed and safe area, which artwork with no blank prints with, and `printFloorDpi` the minimum print resolution its pictures are judged against when a design is made: the template's own, else the tenant's. `fieldKeys` names the field keys its offered fields carry, and `previewUrl` links to its preview, opening with no key for an hour or two. `status` is the template's state now, whichever version is read: `live`, or `paused` once a member has paused it, when customers cannot design on it although its versions are still served. A pause and a resume are each delivered as `template.live_changed`; after a missed delivery, `status` is the state to trust. `poweredBy` is whether the designer shows "Powered by Pixonaut" for the workspace: decided by its plan, then its own setting. `pixel` is whether the designer offers the customer Pixel: the template has Pixel for customers on, and the workspace has not turned it off. A text naming dynamic values, such as `Class of {date.year}`, is answered with them written for today in `tz`, else in the workspace's timezone. The values are `{date.year}`, the current year, `2026`; `{date.nextYear}`, next year, `2027`; `{date.month}`, the month's name, `October`; `{date.academicYear}`, the academic year, starting on 1 August: `2026/27` from August 2026 to July 2027; `{date.dayMonth}`, the day and month, `October 21`; `{date.monthYear}`, the month and year, `October 2026`; `{date.long}`, the full date, `October 21, 2026`; `{date.short}`, the date in digits, `10/21/2026`; `{date.iso}`, the date as ISO 8601 writes it, `2026-10-21`; `{date.custom(<pattern>)}`, the date in a pattern of your own, Unicode's date-pattern letters `y`, `M`, `L`, `d` and `E` with text in single quotes: `{date.custom(d.M.yyyy)}` writes `21.10.2026`, `{date.custom(MMM ''yy)}` writes `Oct '26`. They are written in `lang`, else in the workspace's default language, else English; a value whose name carries a language after a colon, `{date.long:sv}`, is written in it whatever `lang` says. `workspaceLanguage` is the template's workspace's default language, one of the customer-facing languages' codes (English until it chooses one): what the SDK designer is shown in when its mount names no `locale`. `showcases` lists the template's showcases by id and name, the sets of example values its preview and mockup images are drawn with when their `showcase` names one, each with `previewUrl`, a link to its preview that opens with no key as the template's own does. `backgroundSeeThrough` is whether what stands behind the template shows through its background. An SDK names its release in `x-pixonaut-sdk-version`; a release whose renderer cannot draw the template is refused `sdk_outdated`, naming the first release that can.

Naming a `blankId` and `placementId` (both or neither) adds that placement's bounds: its largest and default print box, the box a proof or design naming it and no size prints at (`printWidthMm` × `printHeightMm`, the template's ratio fitted into the default box), and the bleed and safe area it prints with. A client draws its live preview against that box and those margins so it frames the design as the proof does. A named placement that does not resolve, or whose stored sizes are unusable, is refused with `unknown_placement`.

post.description: A designer share link for the template's live version that mounts the designer with what the store sells it on: the blank and placement every proof is fitted to, the store's size menu and its colourway photos, and which size and photo start selected, exactly as the SDK takes them on a store's own page. A front and a back are one link with `sides`: one hosted page with a step per side, each side its own menus and, when it names one, its own template. A link holds two to 10 sides; one with more than 4 is made, and answered with a `sides_over_recommended` warning, since each side is one more step on the page and one more designer in the shopper's browser. The sides of a garment each name a placement on its blank; the sides of an item with no blank, such as a sign or a coaster, name neither `blankId` nor `placementId`, and each is proofed on its template alone. Every side names a blank and its placement or neither, and either every side is on a blank or none is. With a `returnUrl`, approving makes a proof and sends the shopper back to `returnUrl?state=…&proofToken=…` (with `sides`, `returnUrl?state=…&proofToken[front]=…&proofToken[back]=…`), cancelling to `returnUrl?state=…`. `locale` shows the page and the designer in one of `en`, `sv`, `de`, `fr`, `es`, `nl`, `da`, `nb`, `fi`, and the returned `url` then carries `?lang=<locale>`; absent, they are shown in the workspace's default language. `layout` fixes how every side's form lays out its steps, `page` or `steps`; absent, each side's form follows its template's own `form.layout`, and is a page when the template names none. A link carrying `state`, which names one shopper's visit, works for 24 hours; one without it works for the `expiresInDays` it names, or until withdrawn. Every size a side offers is judged as the shopper's approval would judge it, against the side's template and placement, and one it would refuse is refused `print_size_illegal`, naming the side, the size's place in the menu and why. On a blank, the link holds a side for every placement its blank says an order must print: one leaving such a placement out could never be ordered, and is refused `422 placement_unfilled`, naming it. A link through a blank's panel layout is refused `unknown_layout` when the blank has no layout of that name, `layout_out_of_date` when the layout no longer fits the blank at the size the link sells, and `layout_wrong_ratio` when the template's shape is not the layout's canvas, which the template is drawn on. `name` names the link for the workspace, and `designLimit` limits the designs its page makes. The link's address is kept, and the share-link list answers it again as `url`. A member needs what handing out a designer needs; a connected store's integration key, `templates:read` and `designs:update`.

tags.description:
The whole path from a customer's design to a product on its way: the designer
commits a design with the publishable key, and the merchant's server approves
it, prints it and orders it with the secret key, or with the integration key
of a connected store ([Connecting a store](#tag/connecting-a-store)). Each
step is reported as an event to the merchant's webhook endpoints, shown after
the step that emits it.

## 1. The customer commits a design

The designer runs in the customer's browser, on the merchant's storefront, with
the tenant's publishable key. The customer fills in a published template, and
the designer commits what they made with `POST /v1/designs`:

<!-- example: POST /v1/designs request -->
```json
{
  "templateId": "tshirt-basic@2",
  "values": { "name": { "content": "Alexandra" } },
  "blankId": "blank_tshirt",
  "placementId": "front"
}
```

`templateId` is the published template version the customer filled in.
`values` holds what they entered, keyed by the id of the template layer each
value is for, with that layer's properties inside (a text layer's `content`,
for instance). `blankId` and `placementId` name the product and the spot on it
the design is for; send both or neither. A design is checked against its
template when it is committed, and a design that breaks one of the template's
rules is refused with `constraint_violation`.

<!-- example: POST /v1/designs 201 -->
```json
{
  "designId": "6f1c8a2b-3d4e-4f5a-8b6c-7d8e9f0a1b2c",
  "printFloorDpi": 150,
  "lowResolution": []
}
```

The design is now committed, and cannot change. `lowResolution` lists the
pictures that print below `printFloorDpi` at the design's size, the minimum
print resolution the template sets, else your workspace's. It is a warning,
never a refusal. `POST /v1/validate` and `POST /v1/proofs` answer the same
two fields, so a customer can be told before the design is committed. Hand its `designId` to the
merchant's own server with the customer's cart, the way the storefront already
passes an order along.

To show the committed design on its product in the cart, at checkout, on
order pages and in emails, the merchant's server fetches
`GET /v1/designs/{id}/mockup.png`: the design drawn on the blank's photo, as
`GET /t/{id}/mockup.png` draws the template, in the view the customer
previewed it in unless the request names another. Pass the design's
`proofId` as `v` and the image can be kept for good.

<!-- example: webhook design.committed -->
```json
{
  "id": "1790000000000-0192f5a4-7c1e-4d3a-9b6e-2f4c8a1d5e70",
  "type": "design.committed",
  "createdAt": 1790000000000,
  "payload": {
    "designId": "6f1c8a2b-3d4e-4f5a-8b6c-7d8e9f0a1b2c",
    "templateId": "tshirt-basic@2",
    "apiKeyId": "3b2d9c1e-5a4f-4e7d-8c6b-1a0f9e8d7c6b"
  }
}
```

A fulfilment payload, the order data a printshop needs (a material, a
shipping method), can only be attached by the secret or integration key. A
server that needs one commits the design itself: the designer renders a proof
with `POST /v1/proofs`, and the server commits it with `POST /v1/designs`,
sending the proof's `proofToken` and the `fulfilmentPayload`.

## 2. The merchant's server approves it

Once the customer has paid, the merchant's server approves the design with
`POST /v1/designs/{id}/approve` and its secret or integration key. With no
body it approves now:

<!-- example: POST /v1/designs/{id}/approve 200 -->
```json
{ "status": "approved" }
```

<!-- example: webhook design.approved -->
```json
{
  "id": "1790000060000-5d7e1f2a-3b4c-4d5e-8f60-718293a4b5c6",
  "type": "design.approved",
  "createdAt": 1790000060000,
  "payload": {
    "designId": "6f1c8a2b-3d4e-4f5a-8b6c-7d8e9f0a1b2c",
    "approvedVia": "explicit"
  }
}
```

A server that commits the design itself, and has already taken payment, can
approve it in the same call: `"approve": true` on `POST /v1/designs` commits it
approved, so it never waits between two calls, and `design.approved` follows
`design.committed` with `approvedVia` set to `explicit`. It needs the grant
that approves (a secret or integration key holds it); a publishable key
sending it is refused with `forbidden`.

To give the customer a window to change their mind, send `afterDays`:

<!-- example: POST /v1/designs/{id}/approve request -->
```json
{ "afterDays": 14 }
```

<!-- example: POST /v1/designs/{id}/approve 200 -->
```json
{ "status": "scheduled" }
```

The design stays committed, and `design.approval_scheduled` carries the time it
will be approved. When that time comes, `design.approved` follows with
`approvedVia` set to `deadline`, unless the design was rejected first with
`POST /v1/designs/{id}/reject`, which emits `design.rejected`.

<!-- example: webhook design.approval_scheduled -->
```json
{
  "id": "1790000060000-9a8b7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-8c2d-1e0f9a8b7c6d",
  "type": "design.approval_scheduled",
  "createdAt": 1790000060000,
  "payload": {
    "designId": "6f1c8a2b-3d4e-4f5a-8b6c-7d8e9f0a1b2c",
    "approveAfter": 1791209660000
  }
}
```

### Correcting a design before it is ordered

A design that has not been ordered can be corrected with
`PATCH /v1/designs/{id}`. `values` takes the commit's shape and is applied on
top of the design as it is; `expectedRevision` is the `revision` you read:

<!-- example: PATCH /v1/designs/{id} request -->
```json
{
  "values": { "namn": { "content": "Merry Christmas" } },
  "expectedRevision": 1
}
```

<!-- example: PATCH /v1/designs/{id} 200 -->
```json
{
  "revision": 2,
  "edited": true,
  "proofId": "prf_9c1e2d3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b",
  "printFloorDpi": 150,
  "lowResolution": []
}
```

The design is back to `committed`, its approval cleared, and
`design.edited` says so. The correction renders a proof of what the design
now says, `proofId`, which becomes the design's proof: show it to your
customer with `GET /v1/designs/{id}/proof`, and a proof page shows it too.
Values that leave the document as it is write nothing: the answer is
`edited: false` with the current `revision` and proof, and the approval
stands. Approve it again as above; send `expectedRevision`
with the approval to be refused `revision_changed` if someone corrected it
since you read it. A print made before the correction is refused
`print_superseded` when ordered: print the corrected design again once it is
approved.

<!-- example: webhook design.edited -->
```json
{
  "id": "1790000090000-3b4c5d6e-7f8a-4b9c-8d0e-1f2a3b4c5d6e",
  "type": "design.edited",
  "createdAt": 1790000090000,
  "payload": {
    "designId": "6f1c8a2b-3d4e-4f5a-8b6c-7d8e9f0a1b2c",
    "revision": 2
  }
}
```

Once any print of the design has an order, the correction is refused
`not_editable`. `POST /v1/designs/{id}/duplicate` makes a new committed design
from it instead, with `duplicatedFrom` naming the source, and emits
`design.duplicated`. The duplicate waits for you to correct and approve it.

<!-- example: POST /v1/designs/{id}/duplicate 201 -->
```json
{ "designId": "7a2d9b3c-4e5f-4a6b-9c7d-8e9f0a1b2c3d" }
```

### When the customer asks for changes

A customer on a deciding proof page can ask for changes, and your own page can
relay a customer's request with `POST /v1/designs/{id}/request-changes`:

<!-- example: POST /v1/designs/{id}/request-changes request -->
```json
{ "message": "Could the name be larger?", "expectedRevision": 1 }
```

The design stays committed, a scheduled approval is cancelled, and
`design.changes_requested` carries the request's words. `expectedRevision` is
the revision whose proof the customer was shown; a request about a design
corrected since is refused `revision_changed`. Correct the design, or decide
it, and the request is closed; `GET /v1/designs/{id}/review` answers the open
one. The correction's proof is what the customer then decides.

<!-- example: webhook design.changes_requested -->
```json
{
  "id": "1790000095000-4c5d6e7f-8a9b-4c0d-9e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f",
  "type": "design.changes_requested",
  "createdAt": 1790000095000,
  "payload": {
    "designId": "6f1c8a2b-3d4e-4f5a-8b6c-7d8e9f0a1b2c",
    "revision": 1,
    "message": "Could the name be larger?"
  }
}
```

### Sending the customer back to your store to edit

A proof page you hand your customer can send them back to your store once
they have asked for changes, so your store opens the design for them to
correct: see
[Sending the customer back to the store](#tag/sending-the-customer-back-to-the-store).

## 3. Print the approved design

`POST /v1/prints` makes the print files for an approved design:

<!-- example: POST /v1/prints request -->
```json
{ "designId": "6f1c8a2b-3d4e-4f5a-8b6c-7d8e9f0a1b2c" }
```

It answers `202` as soon as the print is reserved, with its `Location`, and
renders it after the answer. The print reads `created` while it renders:

<!-- example: POST /v1/prints 202 -->
```json
{ "printId": "c4d5e6f7-a8b9-4c0d-9e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f", "status": "created" }
```

Read it with `GET /v1/prints/{id}` until it is `completed`, or wait for
`print.completed`, before you order it. To be answered once it has rendered
instead, send `Prefer: wait`: the answer is then a `201` with the print and its
job ticket, which says what to make and how to cut it. The print's ticket says
nothing about any one order: how many copies, your reference and who it ships
to are each order's, added when it is placed.

<!-- example: POST /v1/prints 201 -->
```json
{
  "printId": "c4d5e6f7-a8b9-4c0d-9e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f",
  "jobTicket": {
    "product": {
      "sku": "6f1c8a2b-3d4e-4f5a-8b6c-7d8e9f0a1b2c",
      "tenantId": "acme"
    },
    "artwork": { "templateId": "tshirt-basic@2", "name": "Front" },
    "printArea": {
      "widthMm": 90,
      "heightMm": 50,
      "bleedMm": 3,
      "cutShape": { "type": "path", "d": "M 0 0 L 90 0 L 90 50 L 0 50 Z" }
    },
    "artifact": {
      "file": "PR-2026-000123_6f1c8a2b.pdf",
      "format": "pdf",
      "colorSpace": "DeviceCMYK",
      "iccProfile": "ISOcoated_v2_eci.icc",
      "effectiveDpi": 300,
      "includesBleed": true,
      "trimMarks": false,
      "spotColors": [],
      "spotOutput": "process"
    },
    "manifest": {
      "docHash": "9f2c4e1a",
      "templateVersion": "tshirt-basic@2",
      "rendererVersion": "0.1.0",
      "fontSetHash": "a1b2c3d4",
      "iccProfile": "ISOcoated_v2_eci.icc",
      "renderedAt": "2026-09-21T14:01:40.000Z"
    }
  }
}
```

Cut to `printArea`: it is the geometry the print file was rendered against.
`GET /v1/prints/{id}` reads the print again later.

Printing emits `print.created` when the print is reserved and
`print.completed` when its files are ready. A print that could not be rendered
reads `failed`, with its `failure`, and emits `print.failed` instead; with
`Prefer: wait` the request answers `500` with `render_failed`. A print still
rendering ten minutes after it started is failed too.

<!-- example: webhook print.completed -->
```json
{
  "id": "1790000100000-2b3c4d5e-6f70-4812-9a3b-4c5d6e7f8091",
  "type": "print.completed",
  "createdAt": 1790000100000,
  "payload": { "printId": "c4d5e6f7-a8b9-4c0d-9e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f" }
}
```

## 4. Submit the order

`POST /v1/prints/{id}/orders` sends a completed print to the printshop its
design was committed to, and the order records that connection as
`printshopConnectionId`, with your name for it as `printshopName`. The body
is optional, and every field in it is:

- `quantity` — how many copies; one when left out. It belongs to the order,
  not the print, so one print can be ordered again in another quantity.
- `externalRef` — your own reference for the order, such as your order or
  line id. It is not unique, and `GET /v1/orders?externalRef=` finds every
  order under it.
- `recipient` and `shippingAddress` — who the order is for and where it
  ships. The country is a two-letter ISO code. They are never written to
  logs.
- `variant` — the ref of the blank's variant the shopper chose, such as
  White / M (`GET /v1/blanks/{id}/variants` lists them). A blank with one variant
  needs none; one with several refuses an order naming none
  (`variant_required`), and a variant of another blank or a retired one is
  refused too.

The first four reach the printshop on the job ticket, and a retry of a failed
order carries the same ones and the same variant. The printshop is sent what
it needs for the variant, such as Printful's catalogue variant id, and the
order keeps a copy of the variant as it was placed (`variant`).

<!-- example: POST /v1/prints/{id}/orders request -->
```json
{
  "quantity": 3,
  "externalRef": "ORDER-1042",
  "variant": "v_3f9a1c2b7d4e8a01",
  "recipient": { "name": "Alice Morgan", "email": "alice@example.com" },
  "shippingAddress": {
    "line1": "1 High Street",
    "postalCode": "SW1A 2AA",
    "city": "London",
    "country": "GB"
  }
}
```

<!-- example: POST /v1/prints/{id}/orders 201 -->
```json
{
  "id": "e1f2a3b4-c5d6-4e7f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b",
  "tenantId": "acme",
  "printId": "c4d5e6f7-a8b9-4c0d-9e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f",
  "designId": "6f1c8a2b-3d4e-4f5a-8b6c-7d8e9f0a1b2c",
  "printIds": [
    "c4d5e6f7-a8b9-4c0d-9e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f"
  ],
  "prints": [
    {
      "printId": "c4d5e6f7-a8b9-4c0d-9e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f",
      "designId": "6f1c8a2b-3d4e-4f5a-8b6c-7d8e9f0a1b2c",
      "designRevision": 1,
      "placementId": "front",
      "printedAs": "Front",
      "spotOutput": "process",
      "status": "completed",
      "placementFields": []
    }
  ],
  "quantity": 3,
  "externalRef": "ORDER-1042",
  "recipient": {
    "name": "Alice Morgan",
    "email": "alice@example.com"
  },
  "shippingAddress": {
    "line1": "1 High Street",
    "postalCode": "SW1A 2AA",
    "city": "London",
    "country": "GB"
  },
  "adapter": "printful",
  "shipTo": null,
  "printshopConnectionId": "0b1c2d3e-4f5a-4b6c-8d7e-9f0a1b2c3d4e",
  "printshopName": "Printful",
  "spotOutput": "process",
  "externalOrderRef": "PF-889123",
  "status": "queued",
  "lastError": null,
  "failureKind": null,
  "hold": null,
  "tracking": null,
  "submittedAt": 1790000120000,
  "lastCheckedAt": null,
  "updatedAt": 1790000121000,
  "replacesOrderId": null,
  "replacedByOrderId": null,
  "personalDataErasedAt": null,
  "blankId": "blank_classic_tee",
  "variantRef": "v_3f9a1c2b7d4e8a01",
  "variant": {
    "ref": "v_3f9a1c2b7d4e8a01",
    "options": {
      "Color": "White",
      "Size": "M"
    },
    "fields": [
      {
        "name": "catalogVariantId",
        "value": "4012",
        "source": "own"
      }
    ]
  },
  "printshopAsPlaced": {
    "name": "Printful",
    "adapter": "printful"
  },
  "delivery": null,
  "blank": {
    "name": "Classic tee",
    "optionAxes": [
      "Color",
      "Size"
    ],
    "variants": 12
  }
}
```

A printshop that turns the order down is still a `201`: the order is recorded
with `status: "failed"` and its reason in `lastError`, and `order.failed` is
emitted. A failed order that never reached the printshop can be submitted
again with `POST /v1/orders/{id}/retry`.

<!-- example: webhook order.submitted -->
```json
{
  "id": "1790000120000-7c8d9e0f-1a2b-4c3d-8e4f-5a6b7c8d9e0f",
  "type": "order.submitted",
  "createdAt": 1790000120000,
  "payload": {
    "orderId": "e1f2a3b4-c5d6-4e7f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b",
    "printId": "c4d5e6f7-a8b9-4c0d-9e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f",
    "adapter": "printful",
    "quantity": 3,
    "externalRef": "ORDER-1042",
    "externalOrderRef": null,
    "replacesOrderId": null
  }
}
```

From here the order moves on as the printshop reports it (`queued`,
`printed`, `shipped`), and each move is an `order.status_changed`. Read the
order and its history at any time with `GET /v1/orders/{id}`.

<!-- example: webhook order.status_changed -->
```json
{
  "id": "1790086400000-0f1e2d3c-4b5a-4968-8776-655443322110",
  "type": "order.status_changed",
  "createdAt": 1790086400000,
  "payload": {
    "orderId": "e1f2a3b4-c5d6-4e7f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b",
    "printId": "c4d5e6f7-a8b9-4c0d-9e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f",
    "status": "shipped",
    "previousStatus": "printed"
  }
}
```

An order whose submission timed out has the status `outcome_unknown`: the
printshop may have accepted it, and may be making it now. It is not a failure,
and submitting it again could make the product twice. Ask the printshop what
happened first, then settle it with what it told you. A secret key, a
connected store's integration key or a studio member holding `orders:update`
may do this, and a reason is required:

- The printshop does not have it: mark it `failed`. `POST /v1/orders/{id}/retry`
  then submits it again.
- The printshop has it: mark it `submitted`, with the printshop's own reference
  for it when you were given one, so its status is followed from then on.

<!-- example: PATCH /v1/orders/{id} request -->
```json
{
  "status": "failed",
  "reason": "The printshop has no order under this number."
}
```

An order in `outcome_unknown` that the printshop has given its reference for
can also be cancelled, with `POST /v1/orders/{id}/cancel`, as an order in
`submitted` or `queued` can.

When your customer asks you to erase their personal data, see
[Erasing personal data](#tag/erasing-personal-data).
